claim: A lower g/kg at the dehumidifier outlet than at its inlet shows the unit is removing water; drying-zone g/kg below outside g/kg is context, not proof that drying is working.
reasoning: DERIVED by mass balance: water removed per kg of dry air through the unit equals inlet minus outlet humidity ratio, so a lower outlet reading is direct evidence of removal. The drying-zone versus outside comparison also depends on outdoor conditions, which change independently of drying performance: dry outdoor air can leave a zone that is drying well reading wetter than outside, and cooled or air-conditioned air can read drier than outside while drying stalls. Progress is confirmed by material readings trending to the dry standard.
best_available_source: Psychrometric mass balance on the humidity ratio (ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals, Psychrometrics chapter), cited by name
